problem: Most VLN agents are opaque and give little insight into why a navigation action is chosen; prior explainable VLN methods offer limited interpretability and navigation performance on unseen environments.
motivation: Interpretable decision-making is needed to inspect and trust embodied instruction-following agents. The paper argues that explicit reasoning supervision, in the form of textual explanations and low-level action labels, can improve transparency without hurting navigation, and may even help it.
key_idea: Fine-tune a multimodal LLM-based VLN agent to output the next viewpoint together with a human-readable explanation and a low-level action label, supervised by speaker-style explanations generated from consecutive observations and simulator-derived action labels on R2R trajectories.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that auxiliary reasoning objectives (explanations and action labels) improve unseen-environment navigation over prior explainable VLN methods while keeping strong performance.
method: Visual scene encoder + multimodal LLM: encodes observations and feeds them to an MLLM as the decision-making backbone.
Structured prompts: jointly condition on the instruction, navigation history and candidate viewpoints at each step.
Next-viewpoint prediction: the main navigation objective, selecting among candidate navigable locations.
Explanation supervision: R2R trajectories are augmented with speaker-style action explanations generated from consecutive observations; the model learns to produce them.
Low-level action labels: turn left, turn right, move forward or stop, obtained from the simulator, used as an auxiliary output target.

setting.backbone: visual scene encoder + multimodal LLM (fine-tuned); specific models not stated in abstract
setting.training_data: R2R trajectories augmented with generated speaker-style explanations and simulator action labels
setting.observation: visual observations of candidate viewpoints (panoramic views implied), instruction, navigation history
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (candidate viewpoints) plus descriptive low-level action labels

results: The abstract states that on R2R the approach improves over prior explainable VLN methods on unseen environments while producing interpretable rationales. No numbers are given.
limitations: Abstract only; details and quantitative results could not be verified.
Explanation supervision is generated automatically (speaker-style from observations), so its quality and faithfulness to the model's actual decision process is uncertain.
Evaluated only on R2R according to the abstract.
